top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) is a new chemical modality: a designed small molecule brings a chosen protein to an E3 ligase, turning occupancy-driven pharmacology into event-driven removal. The mechanism is chemically explicit and independently reproduced for two decades, and Handa's cereblon identification ties the PROTAC concept to approved thalidomide-type glues. The citation names both PROTACs and cereblon-dependent glues, so it claims no more than the three names support. Omissions (Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito, Kim) and the lack of an approved bifunctional degrader are real costs, but they concern credit and timing, not whether the chemistry holds. Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (P002) is more mature and cleanly attributed, so it ranks second, ahead of no award.
